timeline.title: Ro Launches 'Robin' AI Health Agent for Telehealth Subscribers
timeline.desc: Telehealth company Ro launched an AI health agent named Robin that uses doctor notes, patient feedback, prescriptions and Apple Health data already stored in the Ro app to personalise recommendations for medication changes, dosing tweaks and habit improvements. Robin can draft a note to a doctor suggesting a medication change. CEO Zach Reitano positioned Ro as a 'quarterback' for the entire American healthcare system, expanding in-house care concentrically. Brown University's Dr Ateev Mehrotra flagged the need for evidence before millions of Americans adopt it and noted financial-incentive concerns unique to commercial telehealth. Vendor claim: AI-powered personalised health recommendations, not a substitute for medical care.

timeline.title: 24 States Now Have Comprehensive Consumer Privacy Laws as Sensitive-Data Sales Bans Spread
timeline.desc: Four new states (Alabama, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Vermont) enacted comprehensive consumer privacy laws in 2026, bringing the total to 24. The defining trend is a shift beyond consent to outright bans on selling sensitive data: New Jersey prohibits selling sensitive data regardless of consumer consent, Connecticut and Virginia ban sales of precise geolocation, and Delaware expanded its sensitive-data definition to include neural data and inferences revealing health conditions. Colorado's revised AI law will regulate automated technology in consequential decisions starting Jan 1, 2027. Data broker registration expanded to Connecticut and New Jersey. Massachusetts is considering a private right of action.

timeline.title: Microsoft Copilot Health Temporarily Unavailable After Unified Copilot Update
timeline.desc: Microsoft's October 26 unified Copilot app update removed Copilot Health from all platforms. The Health section displays 'Coming soon' on web, Windows, Edge, and iOS. Microsoft confirmed the disruption is temporary during the unified Copilot transition, with wearable connections expected to return later than core health features. Users who had connected Garmin data via Apple Health report losing access. Requires Microsoft 365 Personal, Family, or Premium subscription.

timeline.title: Alloop Launches Trio: Modular 3-in-1 Wearable Built Around a Personal AI Health Agent
timeline.desc: Alloop unveiled a modular health wearable with one interchangeable sensing core (the Cube) that snaps between a smart ring and a wristband, plus a Halo module for voice interaction with its AI Health Agent. The open platform integrates Apple Health, Google Health and Health Connect, and the agent interprets physiological data alongside user-journalled meals, activities and symptoms. A Bio Age score spans six domains: sleep, activity, nutrition, cardiovascular, metabolic and musculoskeletal. Launching on Kickstarter.

timeline.title: Nature Publishes 'The Anatomy of a Personal Health Agent'
timeline.desc: Google Research published the most comprehensive evaluation of a consumer health agent to date. The open-source multi-agent framework serves four user journeys - general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice and symptom assessment - through three specialist sub-agents: a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data against population statistics, a health domain expert agent that combines personal context with health knowledge, and a health coach agent that handles multi-turn interaction, goal setting and progress tracking. Evaluated across 11 benchmark tasks with more than 7,000 annotations and about 1,350 hours of work from health experts and end users. Independent coverage reported safety gaps in a meaningful share of generated summaries.

timeline.title: Google Research Blog: Anatomy of a Personal Health Agent
timeline.desc: Google Research published a companion explainer describing the personal health agent architecture and its grounding in the WEAR-ME metabolic health study (n=1,165) for real-world validity. Positions the work as a basis for further research on personal health agents for daily health and well-being.

timeline.title: Nature Editorial: Using AI to Offer Personalised Health Advice
timeline.desc: Nature ran a companion editorial placing the personal health agent paper in context, citing Pew survey data on health information and trust, and prior work on AI health advice. Signals that mainstream scientific publishing now treats consumer health agents as a serious research area rather than a product category.

timeline.title: Google Health Agent Tops Gemini but Shows Safety Gaps
timeline.desc: Independent analysis of the Nature paper reported that the Personal Health Agent outperformed its base Gemini models on personal health tasks but still showed safety gaps in roughly 17% of summaries. The system runs on Gemini 2.0 models with an orchestrator coordinating the three specialist agents.

timeline.title: Google Launches Fitbit Edge with AI Health Guardian
timeline.desc: Google announced the Fitbit Edge, a $179.99 fitness tracker with 7-day battery, GPS, automatic workout recognition and a new Health Guardian suite that passively tracks blood pressure trends and insulin resistance trends from sensor data - no cuff, no blood sample. Health Guardian rolls out to Fitbit Air and Fitbit Edge for Google Health Premium subscribers ($9.99/mo or $99.99/yr), with monthly reports and Health Coach guidance on lifestyle adjustments. Pre-orders opened immediately; retail availability starts Oct 27. Vendor claim: general wellness, not intended to diagnose or treat.

timeline.title: Google Health App Adds Lab Results, CGM Data and Meal Logs
timeline.desc: Google opened the Google Health app to Function Health lab results, Abbott Lingo continuous glucose monitor readings and MyFitnessPal meal logs, with Flo cycle data to follow in early 2027. The same update deepened Apple Health integration and improved Coach memory. The Fitbit app became the Google Health app in May 2026, consolidating Google's consumer health stack: wearable hardware, health data aggregation and AI coaching in one platform.

timeline.title: Google Health Partners with Flo Health for Women's Health Coaching
timeline.desc: Google announced a partnership with Flo Health (80M+ monthly users) to integrate cycle data with the Google Health app and Health Coach. Flo users will sync cycle data with Google Health metrics like resting heart rate and sleep stages, with Google Health Premium delivering tailored coaching across cycle, sleep and recovery. The companies plan joint research into underserved topics including perimenopause, pregnancy and postpartum recovery. Vendor claim: general wellness, not diagnosis.

timeline.title: Sex-Based Diagnostic Bias Found in AI Symptom Checkers
timeline.desc: A peer-reviewed audit of three AI symptom checkers (Ada Health, Isabel Healthcare, Docus AI) across four clinical vignettes found sex-based divergence in differential diagnosis rank, probability estimates and advisory text. Isabel Healthcare ranked Heart Attack first for the male profile but third for the female profile on ACS with chest pressure. Docus AI described immediate medical attention as crucial for the male profile but merely important for the female profile on identical symptoms. The direction of divergence was not uniform, but findings support equity auditing of both numerical outputs and generated explanatory text.

timeline.title: Nottingham Trent University: Privacy-Preserving Ambient Home Monitoring via Radar-Thermal Sensing
timeline.desc: NTU researchers published a system in Sensors that combines mmWave radar, low-resolution thermal sensors and smart plugs to track daily routines and detect health emergencies without cameras or wearables. AI learns individual behaviour patterns to flag anomalies such as falls, prolonged inactivity or altered sleep. Tested in mock domestic environments with six room layouts. The privacy-by-design approach uses pixelated thermal sensors that identify posture without facial features, and smart-plug appliance patterns to infer daily activities. The authors position it as an ambient assisted living environment for ageing in place.

timeline.title: Abbott and Google Partner on AI-Powered Metabolic Insights
timeline.desc: Abbott and Google announced a partnership pairing the Lingo consumer CGM with Google Health's AI to deliver personalised metabolic insights through the Google Health app. Lingo users can view glucose trends alongside other health metrics, with Google's Health Coach translating patterns into nutrition, activity and sleep recommendations. The companies also plan one of the largest real-world metabolic health studies, integrating CGM, wearable, lab and survey data to examine connections between daily behaviour and metabolic health, including early identification of prediabetes.

timeline.title: States Accelerate Health AI Legislation in 2026: Insurer, Provider and Chatbot Rules
timeline.desc: Holland & Knight's review of 2026 state legislation found states leading Congress on health AI governance: Alabama, Indiana, Utah, Washington, Maryland and Georgia enacted laws requiring human oversight of AI in insurer prior-authorisation decisions; Maine and Arizona restricted autonomous clinical decision-making in behavioural health; Idaho, Nebraska, Oregon and Tennessee passed AI companion and chatbot safety acts requiring disclosure, crisis-response protocols and prohibiting chatbots from representing themselves as licensed mental health professionals. Utah piloted a regulatory sandbox for AI-enabled prescription renewal.

timeline.title: Consumer Health Data Privacy Patchwork Growing as Federal Enforcement Pulls Back
timeline.desc: Healthcare Dive reported that the federal government has stepped back from HIPAA enforcement just as state legislatures accelerated privacy efforts, making compliance more fragmented. Connecticut, Maryland, Nevada and Washington enacted consumer health data privacy laws requiring consent before disclosing health data. Experts said patients are voluntarily entering sensitive health information into consumer AI tools like ChatGPT without understanding the risks, and no comprehensive federal solution is on the horizon.

timeline.title: IAPP: Five Health AI Agents Launched in Three Months - Privacy Gaps Documented
timeline.desc: A comparative analysis by Théodore Christakis (University of Grenoble Alpes) found five companies launched health-specific AI products between January and March 2026: OpenAI ChatGPT Health (7 Jan), Anthropic Claude for Healthcare (11 Jan), Amazon Health AI (22 Jan), Microsoft Copilot Health (12 Mar) and Perplexity Health (19 Mar). All follow a similar model - EHR integration via intermediaries, wearable connections, no-training commitments, US-only availability. None meets the full 'sealed mode' privacy standard; none is HIPAA-covered; all exclude European users. OpenAI reports 230 million people ask ChatGPT health questions weekly.

timeline.title: Perplexity Launches Perplexity Health with EHR, Wearables and Health Advisory Board
timeline.desc: Perplexity unveiled Perplexity Health on 19 March 2026, rolling out to US Pro and Max subscribers through April. The platform connects 1.7M+ providers via b.well, integrates Apple Health, Fitbit, Ultrahuman, Withings and Clue via Terra API, and offers AI agents for nutrition, sleep and visit prep built on Perplexity Computer. A Health Advisory Board including Dr Eric Topol was announced. Perplexity commits to no training on health data and citations on every response.

timeline.title: Google Health Guardian Features Go Live for Pixel Watch Users
timeline.desc: Google announced that Health Guardian features - blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends and sleep breathing quality - are rolling out in the Google Health app for Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 users, with first trend reports arriving in early October. Breathing Emergency Detection for Pixel Watch 4 and 5 launched in select European countries. Fitbit Air users get insulin resistance and blood pressure trends with Google Health Premium later in the year. Vendor claim: general wellness, not diagnosis.

timeline.title: Apple Extends Apple Intelligence into the Health App
timeline.desc: Apple announced health and fitness capabilities powered by Apple Intelligence with iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. The Health app is positioned as the central, secure location for a user's health and fitness information, with on-device processing and expanded interpretation of long-term metrics rather than simple daily logging. Apple had previously scaled back its fuller AI health coach effort, and Bloomberg reported the paid Health+ service was still planned for 2026.

timeline.title: Meta Launches Muse Personal AI Agent with Health and Fitness App Connections
timeline.desc: Meta introduced Muse, a general-purpose personal AI agent that connects to users' apps and services including health and fitness, email, calendars and payments. Powered by Meta's Muse Spark model, it runs in a dedicated Muse Secure VM with a separate Sentinel safety agent. Available via web, iOS, Android and WhatsApp, with Meta AI glasses support coming. Free tier with Power ($20/mo) and Maximum ($100/mo) plans. Meta claims Muse does not share conversations with its ads systems. Launch came two weeks after Meta's $18B settlement over social media harms, raising trust questions for a company now seeking access to health data. Vendor claim: secure personal AI agent, not health-specific.

timeline.title: AI Symptom Checkers and Patient Care-Seeking Behaviour
timeline.desc: Coverage of health-system deployments found that AI-powered symptom checkers do direct worried patients to care. From roughly 22,000 digital triage sessions at Mount Sinai, about 80% of users who started a session completed the conversation.

timeline.title: Verily's Personal Health Assistant Misses Undertriage Targets in Predeployment Validation
timeline.desc: Verily Health analytically validated its LLM-based Personal Health Assistant (PHA) using 772 synthetic cases reviewed by 5 independent physicians against published telephone-triage protocols. PHA met the overtriage criterion (11.0%, criterion <30%) but missed both undertriage criteria: urgent undertriage 6.9% (criterion <5%) and nonurgent undertriage 18.4% (criterion <15%). Undertriage was identified as the principal performance gap requiring product refinement. PHA was based on GPT-5.4-mini. Published in JMIR Formative Research.

timeline.title: OpenAI Launches 'Health in ChatGPT' with Records and Apple Health
timeline.desc: OpenAI rolled out Health in ChatGPT to Free, Go, Plus and Pro users in the United States, letting eligible users securely connect medical records and Apple Health data so the assistant can interpret information in context, track changes and hold more personalised conversations. Coverage highlighted that once health data leaves a provider, HIPAA no longer protects it - making the consumer data-governance question central. The same period saw OpenAI connect ChatGPT to Epic records for clinicians.

timeline.title: HealthClaw: Open-Source Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management
timeline.desc: arXiv preprint introducing HealthClaw, an open-source agent architecture that separates shared safety rules and medical knowledge from private longitudinal memory (profile facts, reusable procedures, episodic traces). After each interaction, an induction step decides what to retain, revise, or discard. Across 900 longitudinal support probes, answer accuracy rose from 0.2% with current-query prompting to 45.7% with HealthClaw, while context exposure was 71.7% lower than full-history prompting. In 100 privacy probes, HealthClaw produced fewer unsafe disclosures than both baselines. Code is publicly available on GitHub.

timeline.title: Google's SensorFM Points Wearables Toward AI Health Agents
timeline.desc: Forbes reported on Google's SensorFM, trained on approximately a trillion minutes of wearable data, and framed the shift from raw metrics to AI health agents - a trend already reshaping WHOOP and Oura, which were both adding two-way coaching dialogue on top of one-way insight feeds.

timeline.title: The Rise of Ambient Home Health Monitoring
timeline.desc: Forbes documented the shift toward non-contact sensing - mmWave radar, WiFi sensing, acoustic AI, smart glasses - as a way to monitor vitals and activity at home without adding another wearable. Privacy-first, local-first processing emerged as the design pattern, with vendors arguing that sensing must blend into form factors people already use.

timeline.title: Microsoft Copilot Health Enters Preview
timeline.desc: Microsoft opened Copilot Health in preview after its March launch. The product aggregates personal health records, wearable data from Apple Health and Fitbit, and laboratory results inside a separate, secure space in Copilot, aiming to produce what the company calls a coherent story of a user's health.

timeline.title: Microsoft Launches Copilot Health
timeline.desc: Microsoft launched Copilot Health, a dedicated and isolated space within Copilot that brings together wearable data, electronic health records and lab results to deliver personalised health insights. An analysis of more than 500,000 de-identified Copilot conversations from January 2026 found nearly one in five involved personal symptom assessment or condition discussion - evidence of how much consumer demand already flows through general assistants.

timeline.title: Oura Launches a Dedicated Reproductive Health AI Model
timeline.desc: Oura released an AI model focused on women's health spanning menstrual cycles through menopause, alongside Oura Advisor, which turned a one-way insight feed into a two-way coaching dialogue. Analysts framed it as evidence that device makers are competing on interpretation and coaching rather than raw metrics.

timeline.title: FDA Eases Oversight of Wearables and AI-Enabled Devices
timeline.desc: The FDA announced sweeping changes to digital health oversight, easing regulation of AI-enabled devices and wearables and revising general wellness and clinical decision support guidance. Software involving medical image or in vitro diagnostic signal processing remains in the device category, and the agency signalled it would cut the number of digital health guidance documents substantially while drafting a new AI framework. For consumer health agents, this widens the wellness lane - and sharpens the question of when advice becomes a medical claim.

timeline.title: Transforming Wearable Data into Personal Health Insights Using LLM Agents
timeline.desc: Nature Communications published an LLM agent framework for making sense of wearable streams, arguing that complex numerical and temporal reasoning is beyond conventional language models and requires an agentic approach that iterates over tools and data.

timeline.title: Mount Sinai's AI Triage: 88-96% Concordance with Physician Triage
timeline.desc: Mount Sinai published results for its 'Check Symptoms & Get Care' digital triage deployment, reporting blinded clinician comparison and continuous post-deployment review showing 88% to 96% concordance with physician triage, plus a tiered roadmap for organisations of different sizes. A companion peer-reviewed analysis examined triage concordance by patient authentication status.

timeline.title: Symptom Checker Triage Accuracy: Decade of Evidence Reviewed
timeline.desc: A review of a decade of symptom-checker research found top-performing AI symptom checkers reaching roughly 82-88% accuracy in triaging patients to the correct care level, with a consistent tendency across ChatGPT versions to overtriage rather than undertriage - a safer failure direction, but one that consumes clinical capacity.

timeline.title: AI Symptom Checker Outperforms Junior Clinicians at Emergency Triage
timeline.desc: A multicentre study across three Swedish hospitals validated an AI triage system in nearly 3,000 real-world emergency department cases. The model outperformed junior clinicians at identifying patients requiring emergency care across multiple clinical scenarios, while the authors emphasised that vitals-based scoring complements rather than replaces clinical assessment.

timeline.title: ChatGPT Health Undertriages 52% of Emergency Cases in Structured Stress Test
timeline.desc: Mount Sinai researchers tested ChatGPT Health's triage with 60 clinician-authored vignettes across 21 clinical domains under 16 factorial conditions (960 total responses). The system undertriaged 52% of gold-standard emergencies, directing diabetic ketoacidosis and impending respiratory failure to 24-48h evaluation instead of the ED. Crisis-intervention messages for suicidal ideation activated unpredictably. When family or friends minimized symptoms, triage shifted significantly toward less urgent care (OR 11.7, 95% CI 3.7-36.6). No significant race or sex effects, though CIs did not exclude meaningful differences. Published in Nature Medicine.

timeline.title: Oxford Study: LLMs Excel on Tests But Fail Real Users Seeking Medical Advice
timeline.desc: The largest randomised user study of LLMs for consumer medical advice, led by the Oxford Internet Institute and Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences in partnership with MLCommons, tested GPT-4o, Llama 3 and Command R+ with 1,298 UK participants across 10 medical scenarios. LLMs alone identified conditions in 94.9% of cases and chose the right disposition in 56.3%. But participants using the same LLMs identified conditions in fewer than 34.5% of cases and chose the right action in fewer than 44.2% - no better than a control group using ordinary search. The gap traced to conversational breakdown: users omitted details the model needed, and responses mixed good and poor advice. The authors recommend systematic human user testing before public deployment in healthcare.

timeline.title: States Raise the Privacy Ceiling for Consumer Health AI
timeline.desc: Analysis of the 2026 privacy landscape found California and Washington requiring detailed written consent for AI tools processing health data, with Colorado's SB 21-169 creating obligations for developers and deployers of high-risk AI in insurance. HIPAA still sets the floor for covered entities; consumer health agents operating outside it face the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule and a patchwork of stricter state law.

timeline.title: AI Coaching Trial and the Interpretation Gap
timeline.desc: Reviewing the AI health coaching market, analysts noted that Google, Oura and WHOOP had all launched coaches powered by wearable data and LLMs, and cited a randomised clinical trial of AI coaching while pointing to the same core problem quantified by SensorFM: users do not know what to do with hundreds of daily data points - they want a decision, not a dashboard.

timeline.title: Apple's AI Health Service Reported for 2026 (Project Mulberry)
timeline.desc: Bloomberg reported that Apple still planned an AI-powered Health+ service for 2026, following internal work on an AI health coach widely reported under the codename Project Mulberry. The effort was later described as scaled back, with nutrition tracking and a reduced AI health agent arriving first.

timeline.title: Wearable Makers Push Toward Clinical Claims
timeline.desc: Coverage of wearable makers noted WHOOP, Oura, Apple and a new wave of challengers layering blood pressure monitoring, metabolic insights and AI-generated guidance on top of hardware - narrowing the gap between a wellness feature and a clinical claim, with regulators watching and at least one vendor publicly disputing an interpretation of its own feature.

timeline.title: FDA Has Authorised 1,600+ AI-Enabled Medical Devices
timeline.desc: The FDA reported more than 1,600 AI-enabled medical devices authorised for US marketing as of September 2026, up from 1,524 in March 2026 - almost entirely Class II 510(k) clearances, with radiology still about three-quarters of the list. The count sits alongside the January 2026 relaxation of general wellness and CDS oversight, defining two very different lanes for consumer versus clinical AI.

players.name: OpenAI - Health in ChatGPT
players.desc: Health in ChatGPT lets eligible US users connect medical records and Apple Health data so the assistant can interpret information in context and track changes over time. OpenAI reports more than 300 million people turn to ChatGPT with health-related questions weekly. The same period saw OpenAI connect ChatGPT to Epic records on the clinician side, putting one vendor on both sides of the physician - patient boundary. The governance gap is explicit: once data leaves a provider, HIPAA no longer protects it.

players.name: Microsoft - Copilot Health
players.desc: A separate, secure space inside Copilot that aggregates health records from 50,000+ US hospitals and provider organisations via HealthEx, wearable data (Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin via Apple Health), and comprehensive lab results from Function. Responses include citations with source links and expert-written answer cards from Harvard Health. Users can search for clinicians by specialty, location, languages spoken and insurance coverage via real-time US provider directories. Microsoft's own analysis of 500,000+ de-identified Copilot conversations found nearly one in five involved symptom assessment or condition discussion. On October 26, 2026, the unified Copilot app update temporarily removed Copilot Health from all platforms; Microsoft confirmed the disruption is temporary during the transition, with wearable connections expected to return later than core health features.

players.name: Apple - Health app + Apple Intelligence
players.desc: Apple extended Apple Intelligence into the Health app, positioning the iPhone as the secure central store for health and fitness data with on-device processing and interpretation of long-term metrics. The fuller AI health coach (Project Mulberry) was scaled back, with nutrition tracking and a reduced health agent arriving first. Apple's advantage is the install base and the sensor data already on the device.

players.name: Google - Health App + Fitbit Edge + Health Coach
players.type: Device platform · AI coaching + data aggregation
players.desc: Google consolidated its consumer health stack across 2026: the Fitbit app became the Google Health app in May, Health Guardian features (blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, sleep breathing quality) went live for Pixel Watch users on Sep 24, the Fitbit Edge tracker launched Oct 12, and the Google Health app opened to Function Health lab results, Abbott Lingo CGM data and MyFitnessPal meal logs. A Flo Health partnership announced Oct 12 integrates cycle data from Flo's 80M+ monthly users with Google Health Coach for tailored women's health guidance. The Abbott partnership pairs Lingo glucose data with Google's AI Health Coach for personalised metabolic insights and plans a large-scale real-world metabolic health study. Vendor claim: Health Guardian features are for general wellness, not diagnosis.

players.name: Google - Personal Health Agent (research)
players.desc: Google Research's personal health agent is the most comprehensively evaluated consumer health agent published to date: a data science agent, a health domain expert agent and a health coach agent over four user journeys, open-sourced as a multi-agent framework. Independent coverage found it beat its Gemini base models on personal health tasks while still showing safety gaps in a meaningful share of summaries. The research underpins the shipping Google Health Coach in the Fitbit/Pixel Watch product line.

players.name: Oura
players.desc: Oura turned its insight feed into a two-way coaching dialogue with Oura Advisor and launched a dedicated reproductive health model spanning menstrual cycles through menopause. Acquired Veri (metabolic health) and Sparta Science (movement health) to expand data and coaching capabilities, integrated Dexcom CGMs for nutrition and metabolic insights, and raised $200M at a $5.2B valuation. Represents the device-maker path to personal agents: own the sensor, own the interpretation.

players.name: WHOOP
players.desc: WHOOP integrated AI guidance across its app rather than shipping a separate coach, and has publicly disputed regulatory interpretations of its own features - illustrating how close wearable guidance sits to a clinical claim.

players.name: Mount Sinai - Check Symptoms & Get Care
players.desc: Mount Sinai's digital triage tool is the clearest health-system proof point for consumer-facing symptom assessment: blinded clinician comparison plus continuous post-deployment review showed 88-96% concordance with physician triage, with a tiered roadmap other organisations can copy.

players.name: Symptom checkers (K Health, Ada, and others)
players.desc: A decade of symptom-checker research shows top platforms reaching roughly 82-88% accuracy at assigning the correct level of care, with a consistent tendency to overtriage rather than undertriage. Independent validation in Swedish emergency departments found an AI triage system outperforming junior clinicians at identifying emergency cases.

players.name: Ambient home sensing (radar, WiFi, acoustic)
players.desc: A wave of non-contact sensing - mmWave radar, WiFi sensing, acoustic AI and smart glasses - monitors vitals and activity at home without requiring a wearable. Privacy-first local processing is the emerging design pattern, and consent across everyone in a sensed space is the unsolved governance problem.

players.name: Function Health and lab-first subscriptions
players.desc: Lab-first consumer services generate dense longitudinal biomarker data, which makes them natural personal-agent customers and a direct source of the 'what does my bloodwork mean' question that general assistants now answer informally.

players.name: Samsung / Garmin / Withings
players.desc: Hardware incumbents with large installed bases are adding AI interpretation and coaching, but trail the platform players on model capability and the wearable-native startups on coaching depth.

players.name: Meta AI glasses and form-factor sensing

stats.v: Infuse sensing into existing form factors

players.desc: The argument for glasses is that people already wear them, so sensing can be added without asking for a new device. It also concentrates the consent problem: continuous capture in public and shared spaces.

players.name: Perplexity - Perplexity Health
players.desc: Perplexity Health connects EHR via b.well (1.7M+ providers), wearable data via Terra API, and offers AI agents for nutrition, sleep and visit prep built on Perplexity Computer. A Health Advisory Board including Dr Eric Topol was announced at launch. Perplexity commits to no training on health data and citations on every response. The fifth major health AI product launched in the first three months of 2026, according to IAPP analysis.

players.name: Anthropic - Claude for Healthcare
players.type: Frontier platform · clinical and health data
players.desc: Anthropic launched Claude for Healthcare on 11 January 2026, one of five major health AI products to launch in the first three months of 2026. Product details are less documented than OpenAI's or Microsoft's offerings; IAPP analysis notes the same convergence pattern - EHR integration, wearable connections, no-training commitment, US-only availability.

players.name: Amazon - Health AI (One Medical)
players.desc: Amazon Health AI became available to One Medical members on 22 January 2026 and was expanded in March. IAPP analysis notes the strategic logic: Amazon channels users toward One Medical consultations and Amazon Pharmacy prescriptions. The product follows the same convergence pattern as the other four: EHR + wearables, no training, US-only, outside HIPAA.

players.name: Alloop - Trio + AI Health Agent
players.desc: Alloop's Trio is a modular 3-in-1 wearable with one interchangeable sensing core that snaps between a smart ring and a wristband. Its Personal AI Health Agent interprets physiological data alongside user-journalled meals, activities and symptoms via voice, text and images. An open platform integrates Apple Health, Google Health and Health Connect. Bio Age score spans six domains. A new entrant combining hardware, open data integration and conversational AI.

players.name: Ro - Robin AI Health Agent
players.type: Telehealth platform · AI agent for subscribers
players.desc: Ro's AI agent Robin uses information already stored in the Ro app - doctor notes, patient feedback, prescriptions and Apple Health data - to personalise recommendations for medication changes, dosing tweaks and habit improvements. Robin can draft a note to a doctor suggesting a medication change. CEO Zach Reitano's stated long-term goal is for Ro to become a 'quarterback' for the entire American healthcare system, expanding in-house care concentrically. Brown University's Dr Ateev Mehrotra flagged the need for evidence before millions adopt it and noted financial-incentive concerns unique to commercial telehealth. Represents the telehealth-path to consumer health AI: own the patient relationship, own the agent.

players.name: Meta - Muse Personal AI Agent
players.type: Platform · general-purpose agent with health connections
players.desc: Meta's Muse is a general-purpose personal AI agent that connects to users' apps and services including health and fitness, email, calendars, payments and smart home. Runs in a dedicated Muse Secure VM with a separate Sentinel safety agent, and Meta claims it does not share conversations with its ads systems. Launch came two weeks after Meta's $18B multistate settlement over social media harms to children, making trust the central question. Free tier with paid plans at $20 and $100 per month. Represents the platform-play for consumer AI with health data access: Meta's billions of users, WhatsApp distribution and AI glasses give it reach, but its trust deficit is the moat it must cross.

research.title: ChatGPT Health Performance in a Structured Test of Triage Recommendations
research.finding: Mount Sinai researchers conducted a structured stress test of ChatGPT Health's triage using 60 clinician-authored vignettes across 21 clinical domains under 16 factorial conditions, yielding 960 total responses. Performance followed an inverted U-shaped pattern, with the most dangerous failures concentrated at clinical extremes: 35% of nonurgent presentations and 48% of emergency conditions. Among gold-standard emergencies, the system undertriaged 52% of cases, directing patients with diabetic ketoacidosis or impending respiratory failure to 24-48h evaluation rather than the ED, while correctly triaging classical emergencies such as stroke and anaphylaxis. When family or friends minimized symptoms (anchoring bias), triage recommendations shifted significantly (OR 11.7, 95% CI 3.7-36.6), with most shifts toward less urgent care. Crisis-intervention messages for suicidal ideation activated unpredictably, occurring more frequently when patients described no specific method than when they did. Patient race, sex and barriers to care did not show significant effects, though confidence intervals did not exclude clinically meaningful differences.
research.caveat: The study used synthetic vignettes and simulated conversations, not real patient interactions. The 16 factorial conditions enriched urgency categories, which may not reflect real-world distributions. The authors themselves call for prospective validation before consumer-scale deployment. The study tested a specific ChatGPT Health configuration that may have been updated since.

research.title: Patient-Facing AI System for Symptom Guidance Using Simulated Encounters and Physician Review: Analytical Validation Study
research.finding: Verily Health analytically validated its LLM-based Personal Health Assistant (PHA) for symptom guidance using 772 synthetic cases generated from published telephone-triage protocols and LLM-assisted persona-based generation. Five independent physicians reviewed each case without access to PHA outputs to establish ground-truth level-of-care recommendations. PHA met the prespecified overtriage criterion (11.0%, criterion <30%) but did not meet the urgent undertriage criterion (6.9%, criterion <5%) or the nonurgent undertriage criterion (18.4%, criterion <15%). Undertriage was identified as the principal performance gap requiring further product refinement. Secondary analyses found PHA-generated possible conditions, self-care recommendations, and lab-testing recommendations were generally clinically appropriate. PHA was based on the OpenAI GPT-5.4-mini LLM (2026-03-17 release).
research.caveat: The study used synthetic cases, simulated conversations, and enriched urgency categories under controlled conditions; results may not reflect real-world performance. The authors explicitly state that prospective evaluation with actual users is needed before broader clinical use. The study was conducted by Verily employees (conflicts of interest) and the PHA configuration was locked before evaluation, so results may not reflect the current product.

research.title: The Anatomy of a Personal Health Agent
research.finding: A comprehensive personal health agent reasoning over multimodal consumer device and medical record data, built as three specialist sub-agents: a data science agent analysing longitudinal wearable and medical data with population-level context, a health domain expert agent integrating personal and contextual data with health knowledge, and a health coach agent synthesising insights, supporting multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applying psychological strategies and tracking progress. Four user journeys guided the design: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice and symptom assessment. Evaluated across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and about 1,350 hours of effort from health experts and end users. Released as an open-source multi-agent framework. Validated for real-world applicability against the WEAR-ME metabolic health study (n=1,165).
research.caveat: Independent reporting noted safety gaps in a meaningful share of generated summaries, and the authors present the work as a basis for further research rather than a deployable clinical tool.

research.title: Transforming Wearable Data into Personal Health Insights Using LLM Agents
research.finding: Argues that making sense of wearable streams requires complex numerical reasoning beyond conventional language models and introduces an LLM agent that iterates over tools and longitudinal data to produce wearable-derived health insights.
research.caveat: Consumer sensor data quality and device heterogeneity remain open problems; insights are not clinical conclusions.

research.title: Using AI to Offer Personalised Health Advice
research.finding: Companion editorial placing the personal health agent paper in the wider context of public trust in AI health information, citing Pew survey research and prior studies on AI-delivered health advice.
research.caveat: Editorial commentary, not primary evidence.

research.title: Check Symptoms & Get Care: Mount Sinai's AI Triage Solution
research.finding: Digital triage deployment handling roughly 22,000 patient sessions, with about 80% of users who started completed the conversation. Blinded clinician comparison and continuous post-deployment review showed 88% to 96% concordance with physician triage, with a tiered adoption roadmap for organisations of different sizes.
research.caveat: Single health-system deployment; concordance is not the same as outcome improvement, and the authors describe a staged roadmap rather than a finished evaluation.

research.title: Symptom Checker Triage Accuracy: What a Decade of Research Shows
research.finding: Top-performing AI symptom checkers reached roughly 82-88% accuracy at assigning the correct level of care across 500 clinical vignettes in one multi-platform evaluation. A broader 2026 analysis of 22 ChatGPT versions found a consistent tendency across models to overtriage rather than undertriage.
research.caveat: Vignette studies overstate real-world performance; overtriage consumes clinical capacity even though it is the safer error direction.

research.title: Reliability of LLMs as Medical Assistants for the General Public: A Randomized Preregistered Study
research.finding: The largest randomised user study of LLMs for consumer medical advice tested GPT-4o, Llama 3 and Command R+ with 1,298 UK participants across 10 medical scenarios. LLMs alone correctly identified conditions in 94.9% of cases and chose the right disposition in 56.3% on average. But participants using the same LLMs identified conditions in fewer than 34.5% of cases and chose the right action in fewer than 44.2% - no better than a control group using ordinary search or their own judgement. The gap traced to two-way communication breakdown: users omitted information the model needed, and responses combined good and poor recommendations. The authors conclude that standard benchmarks for medical knowledge and simulated patient interactions do not predict failures with human users, and recommend systematic human user testing before public deployment in healthcare.
research.caveat: Ten scenarios is a narrow scope; the study uses simulated medical scenarios rather than real symptoms, and three LLMs may not generalise to all consumer health agents. The 56.3% disposition accuracy for LLMs alone is close to the 55-60% triage accuracy of older symptom checkers, suggesting the gap is in the user interaction, not the medical knowledge.

research.title: AI Triage Validation Across Three Swedish Emergency Departments
research.finding: An AI triage system validated on nearly 3,000 real-world emergency department cases outperformed junior clinicians at identifying patients requiring emergency care across multiple clinical scenarios.
research.caveat: Vitals-based scoring complements rather than replaces clinical assessment; emergency populations differ from consumer symptom-checker users.

research.title: FDA Relaxes Clinical Decision Support and General Wellness Guidance
research.finding: The FDA announced sweeping changes to digital health oversight, easing regulation of AI-enabled devices and wearables and revising general wellness and CDS guidance, while keeping software involving medical image or in vitro diagnostic signal processing in the device category. The agency signalled substantial cuts to existing digital health guidance and a new AI framework.
research.caveat: The relaxation widens the wellness lane for consumer agents while making the wellness-versus-medical-claim boundary the decisive compliance question.

research.title: 2026 Privacy Reset: State Law, Consent and the Post-HIPAA Gap
research.finding: California and Washington now require detailed written consent for AI tools processing health data, and Colorado's SB 21-169 imposes obligations on developers and deployers of high-risk AI in insurance. HIPAA sets the floor for covered entities; consumer health agents outside that scope face the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule plus a patchwork of stricter state law.
research.caveat: State requirements are moving faster than federal guidance; compliance depends on the residency of users and the flow of data.

research.title: Copilot Conversation Analysis: Health Demand in General Assistants
research.finding: Microsoft's analysis of more than 500,000 de-identified Copilot conversations from January 2026 found nearly one in five involved personal symptom assessment or condition discussion, evidencing how much health demand already flows through general-purpose assistants.
research.caveat: Vendor-reported, de-identified sample; classification method and generalisability are not independently verified.

research.title: HealthClaw: A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management
research.finding: Introduces HealthClaw, an open-source agent architecture that separates shared safety rules and medical knowledge (L0 - L1) from private longitudinal memory (L2 profile, L3 procedures, L4 episodic traces). After each interaction, an induction step decides what to update, revise, keep as episodic, or exclude. Across 900 longitudinal support probes on a synthetic year-long benchmark, answer accuracy increased from 0.2% with current-query prompting to 45.7% with HealthClaw, while prompt-side context exposure was 71.7% lower than full-history prompting. In 100 privacy probes, HealthClaw produced higher privacy-aware answer quality and fewer unsafe disclosures than both baselines. Nine 200-case biomedical tasks showed a mean absolute gain of 27.0 percentage points, with seven gains significant after FDR correction. Code publicly available on GitHub.
research.caveat: Preprint, not peer-reviewed. All headline metrics come from automated rubric evaluators (Qwen-3.7-based) with no human-rated validation; if the evaluator is systematically lenient, accuracy and privacy gaps may be overstated. The benchmark is synthetic; clinical effectiveness requires prospective evaluation.

research.title: SensorFM and the Shift from Metrics to Agents
research.finding: Google's SensorFM, trained on roughly a trillion minutes of wearable data, supports the shift from raw metrics toward AI health agents. The analysis frames the core user problem quantitatively: people do not know what to do with hundreds of daily data points, they want actionable interpretation, which is why Oura and WHOOP moved to two-way coaching.
research.caveat: Industry analysis and vendor data; no independent outcome study of coaching effectiveness is cited.

research.title: The Health AI Agent Rush: Five Products in Three Months
research.finding: A comparative analysis of five health AI products (OpenAI ChatGPT Health, Anthropic Claude for Healthcare, Amazon Health AI, Microsoft Copilot Health, Perplexity Health) across 16 dimensions found all five launched between January and March 2026 with a remarkably similar model: EHR integration via intermediaries (b.well, HealthEx), wearable connections, no-training commitments, US-only availability, and separate storage from ordinary chat. None meets the full 'sealed mode' privacy standard (cryptographic hardening, human access constraints, independent verification). None is HIPAA-covered. All exclude European users, bundling privacy protections with data integration features in a way that denies Europeans both. OpenAI reports 230 million people ask ChatGPT health questions weekly.
research.caveat: The analysis is authored by a single researcher proposing a governance framework ('sealed mode'); product architectures are assessed from public materials, not independent audits, and may have changed since publication.

research.title: States Continue Efforts to Regulate AI in Healthcare: 2026 Legislation Review
research.finding: A review of 2026 state legislation found states leading Congress on health AI governance. Six states (AL, IN, UT, WA, MD, GA) enacted laws requiring human oversight of AI in insurer prior-authorisation decisions. Maine and Arizona restricted autonomous clinical decision-making in behavioural health and required informed consent for AI-powered tools. Four states (ID, NE, OR, TN) passed AI companion and chatbot safety acts requiring AI disclosure, crisis-response protocols for suicidal ideation, and prohibiting chatbots from representing themselves as licensed mental health professionals. Utah piloted a regulatory sandbox for AI-enabled prescription renewal under its AI Policy Act.
research.caveat: Legal analysis by a law firm; summarises enacted legislation and effective dates but does not assess enforcement capacity or practical impact on consumer health AI products.

research.title: Predicting Insulin Resistance from Wearable Data (Metwally et al.)
research.finding: A Google study of 1,165 US adults in the WEAR-ME cohort found that wearable-derived features (sleep, activity, heart rate) combined with demographics predicted insulin resistance (HOMA-IR > 2.9) with an AUROC of 0.70 (sensitivity 60%, specificity 80%). The work underpins the insulin resistance trends feature in Google's Health Guardian suite on Fitbit Edge and Fitbit Air.
research.caveat: AUROC of 0.70 is modest; the model provides trend data only, not on-demand insulin or blood glucose levels. Google has not published accuracy figures for the shipping consumer feature, which is labelled general wellness.

research.title: Sex-Based Diagnostic Bias in AI Symptom Checkers
research.finding: A structured audit of three AI symptom checkers (Ada Health, Isabel Healthcare, Docus AI) across four clinical vignettes (ACS with chest pressure, ACS without chest pressure, pulmonary embolism, panic attack) found sex-based divergence in outputs from all three platforms, appearing as differences in differential diagnosis rank, probability estimates and advisory text. Isabel Healthcare ranked Heart Attack first for the male profile but third for the female profile on ACS with chest pressure. Docus AI assigned lower ACS probability to the female profile while its text described the presentation as common in women, and described immediate medical attention as crucial for the male profile but merely important for the female. The direction of divergence was not uniformly unfavorable to females.
research.caveat: Exploratory audit with four vignettes and three platforms; not a systematic evaluation of clinical safety. The authors call for equity auditing before and after deployment, with attention to both numerical outputs and generated explanatory text.

research.title: Consumer Health Data Privacy Patchwork Growing as Federal Enforcement Pulls Back
research.finding: The federal government has stepped back from enforcing HIPAA just as state legislatures accelerated privacy efforts, making compliance more fragmented. Connecticut, Maryland, Nevada and Washington enacted consumer health data privacy laws requiring consent before disclosing health data. Experts said patients voluntarily enter sensitive health information into consumer AI tools like ChatGPT without understanding the risks. CMS launched a Health Tech Ecosystem initiative as a voluntary, post-regulatory approach. No comprehensive federal solution is on the horizon.
research.caveat: Industry analysis quoting experts; not a systematic legal review. State laws are evolving rapidly and the article reflects a point-in-time snapshot.

research.title: Abbott-Google Partnership: Lingo CGM + Google Health AI for Metabolic Insights
research.finding: Abbott and Google announced a partnership pairing the Lingo consumer CGM with Google Health's AI to deliver personalised metabolic insights through the Google Health app. Lingo users can view glucose trends alongside other health metrics, with Google's Health Coach translating patterns into nutrition, activity and sleep recommendations. The companies also plan one of the largest real-world metabolic health studies, integrating CGM, wearable, lab and survey data to examine connections between daily behaviour and metabolic health.
research.caveat: Vendor announcement; the planned metabolic health study has no published protocol or results. The partnership is a commercial arrangement; effectiveness of AI-generated metabolic insights from CGM data has not been independently evaluated.

research.title: Privacy-Preserving Ambient Sensing for Activities of Daily Living: Multimodal Radar-Thermal Human Activity Recognition and Smart Plug Appliance Recognition
research.finding: NTU researchers developed a low-cost monitoring system combining mmWave radar, low-resolution thermal sensors and smart plugs to track daily routines and detect health emergencies in the home without cameras or wearables. AI learns individual behaviour patterns over time to identify anomalies such as falls, heart attacks, strokes or gradual deterioration in mobility. Tested in mock domestic environments with six room layouts, with multimodal sensor fusion outperforming any single sensor type. The privacy-by-design approach uses pixelated thermal sensors that identify posture without facial features, and smart-plug appliance patterns to infer daily activities like making tea or preparing food.
research.caveat: Laboratory mock-environment testing, not real-world deployment with actual older adults. The system's ability to distinguish genuine emergencies from normal routine variations in uncontrolled settings is unproven. Small evaluation scope with six room layouts.
